chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said:

I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) bid farewell to the House. So when he wanted to exit from the door of the Masjid, he fell prostrate. Then he stood up, faced the Ka'bah, and said: 'O Allah, I return upon that there is no god except You.'

key_terms.أَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ: There is no god except You
key_terms.الْمَسْجِد: The Masjid (specifically Masjid al-Haram in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual and supplication for bidding farewell to the Ka'bah in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the ritual of *Tawaf al-Wada'* (farewell circumambulation), where Imam Al-Hasan (AS) demonstrated profound reverence by prostrating at the mosque's exit before reciting a concise declaration of monotheism. This practice underscores the spiritual significance of concluding one's pilgrimage with humility and reaffirmation of faith, a tradition deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence and devotional practice.
